scope: Accepted received-source contention propagation and bounded original-observation recovery. Controlled local Core/UDP tests; production same-Participant fanout is a separate integration checkpoint.
problem: Concurrent recipients share one actual SIP source. Accepted source metadata used bool current checks that turned temporary registry/session/SIP source contention into definitive Refused, causing either native recipient to remain not_started. Earlier actual duplex/fanout attempts froze both recipients but submitted only one; this was not Participant deduplication.
change: Accepted Stamp validation preserves capture errors, including NotReady, instead of collapsing busy metadata into retirement. Prequeue source admission remains strict and counts busy input as dropped; original audience is never recaptured.

The received source wrapper uses physical poll results for its passive hint and accepts temporary NotReady/Pending only for scheduling. Each actual IO poll separately requires exact live registration/binding and physical source custody. It no longer invokes bool physical.current before physical.poll.

Existing Core bounded waits, source ownership, fresh authorization, original expiry, source observation/operation identity, native recipient fences and captured outcome rules remain in force. No blanket retry of Refused and no serial fanout workaround.

assertions: Accepted source under session metadata contention returns NotReady; fresh unaccepted input during the same contention drops and is not queued later. Release prepares and delivers the original observation.

Physical NotReady and Pending preserve the exact accepted route; while busy there is no host policy acquisition or UDP output. Release recovers; cancellation and deadline remain bounded without output or policy acquisition.

Definitive physical refusal and dropped source registration remain Refused; source grants are not retained idle. Existing source replacement, retirement, original privacy/credential and audience/member ABA cases remain covered.
